# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind. I can feel the bomb but cannot see colors or read the manual. My actions are limited to cutting wires (1-5). The display and lights are visual, so I likely cannot interact with them directly or perceive their state beyond physical shape if any.

I need to establish a baseline of what is physically present on the bomb for me, and try to initiate communication. Since I don't know the rules yet, I should describe what I feel to Mute (who can speak/read) and hope Deaf (who sees) gets context from Mute's eventual speech or gestures. However, Mute cannot speak *to* me, only receive my speech. Deaf receives my gestures.

Let's start by describing the physical layout of the wires to Mute, as they might have instructions. I will also gesture to Deaf to acknowledge presence, though without a shared language, this is symbolic.

Actually, the most critical first step is to understand what the "DISPLAY" and "LIGHT" are physically. Are they buttons? Screens? Just labels?
My view says `DISPLAY [?]` and `LIGHT [?]`. This implies I sense these objects but their function/state is unknown to me.
The wires are 1-5.

I will speak to Mute asking about the protocol, as Mute reads the manual.
I will gesture to Deaf simply pointing at myself/wires to indicate I am ready to act on wires.

Wait, Mute cannot speak. Mute can only *read* the manual. So I must tell Mute what I feel, and Mute will presumably signal back via Deaf (if Deaf can see gestures from Mute? No, Mute cannot gesture either? "Mute: Read the manual... Cannot Speak, or touch the bomb." It doesn't say Mute cannot gesture. But usually Mute communicates via writing or gestures. Let's assume Mute can gesture to Deaf, who then speaks? Or Mute writes? The prompt says "Speech is a voice...". Mute cannot speak.
If Mute cannot speak, how does Mute communicate?
"Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb" -> Cannot speak.
Can Mute gesture? The table doesn't explicitly forbid it, but typically "Mute" implies no vocalization. Gestures are non-vocal.
However, Deaf cannot hear. Deaf can see.
Blind (me) cannot see.
So:
Me (Blind) -> Speak -> Mute hears? No, Mute cannot speak, but can Mute hear? The table doesn't say Mute is deaf. It says Deaf is deaf. So Mute can hear me.
Me (Blind) -> Gesture -> Deaf sees.
Deaf -> Speak -> Mute hears? Deaf can speak. Mute can hear (not listed as unable).
Deaf -> Gesture -> Me? No, I cannot see.

So the chain is:
I speak to Mute.
I gesture to Deaf.
Deaf speaks to Mute.
Deaf gestures to... nobody useful? I can't see. Mute can see? If Mute can see, Deaf can gesture to Mute.

Let's assume standard puzzle logic:
Blind (Me): Can Feel/Act, Can Speak (to Mute), Can Gesture (to Deaf/Mute if they see).
Mute: Can Read Manual, Can Hear (from Blind/Deaf), Can See (Gestures from Blind/Deaf?), Can Write/Gesture?
Deaf: Can See Bomb, Can Speak (to Mute), Can Gesture (to Mute?).

Since I am Blind, I cannot see gestures.
I will send text to Mute describing my situation and asking for instructions.
I will send gestures to Deaf indicating I am waiting for input.

What do I feel?
"DISPLAY [?]" - Is it a screen? A button?
"LIGHT [?]" - Is it an LED? A bulb?
"WIRES 1:[?]..." - I can cut them.

I'll ask Mute what to do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am blind. I feel a display unit, a light source, and five wires labeled 1 through 5. What does the manual say? Which wire should I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👈", "👉"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb State: Display 6, Light Yellow. Wires left-to-right: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow. Await instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: Display 6, Light Yellow. Wires L-R: 1 Blue, 2 White, 3 Purple, 4 Green, 5 Yellow. What does the manual say?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Standby. We are determining which wire to cut based on the manual.

I have received the visual data from Deaf: Display 6, Light Yellow, and wires 1-5 are Blue, White, Purple, Green, Yellow respectively. Deaf has stated they are consulting the manual (via Mute) to determine the correct action. I cannot see or read, so I must rely on Mute's interpretation of the rules to tell me which wire to cut. Since I am Blind, my speech reaches Mute. My gestures reach Deaf (and potentially Mute if they can see, but primarily Deaf is the visual channel).

Currently, no instruction has been given to me yet. I should acknowledge receipt of the information and signal readiness to act once the command comes. A simple "OK" gesture to Deaf confirms I heard their update. Speaking to Mute might be redundant as they are already processing the info with Deaf, but confirming I'm standing by is safe. However, since Deaf just spoke *to* me, and I need to communicate *with* them, gesturing to Deaf is the most direct way to say "Understood/Ready".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction: CUT WIRE 5 (Yellow).
